The Honey AI Voice Receptionist loads company information from a Word document, splits it into overlapping chunks, embeds them with all-MiniLM-L6-v2, and stores them in ChromaDB. It retrieves relevant chunks for each question and asks Groq to generate a grounded response. Users can type, or speak through Whisper transcription; pyttsx3 reads responses aloud.

The uploaded project uses Python, python-docx, NumPy, SciPy, sounddevice, pyttsx3, OpenAI Whisper, ChromaDB, python-dotenv, SentenceTransformers, LangChain text splitters, and Groq. The embedding model is all-MiniLM-L6-v2; Whisper uses tiny.en. BeautifulSoup is imported but isn’t used in the supplied implementation.

source: untitled15.py, VoiceRecorderSTT and speak_text; website implementation
text: In the Python project, sounddevice records microphone audio at 16 kHz, Whisper tiny.en transcribes it, and pyttsx3 speaks the response at a configured rate of 160 words per minute. This website instead uses your browser’s speech recognition and speech synthesis when supported. Browser dictation requires microphone permission.

The project splits text into 400-character chunks with 60-character overlap. SentenceTransformer all-MiniLM-L6-v2 produces 384-dimensional embeddings stored in a persistent ChromaDB collection. Each query retrieves up to three chunks to provide context for Groq.

For the original Python project, install requirements.txt, place the Word knowledge base beside the script, and set GROQ_API_KEY in a .env file. A first-run bug needs correcting: initialize_vector_store must return (collection, embedding_model) after both new indexing and existing-collection paths; the uploaded version only returns in the else branch. Microphone access and downloadable model files are also needed for voice mode.

Customer Churn & NLP Risk Analytics is a Streamlit app comparing Logistic Regression and Random Forest, with exploratory charts, confusion matrices, classification reports, feature importance, individual prediction, and batch CSV export. Numeric features are tenure, monthly charges and support tickets; contracts are one-hot encoded; feedback uses TF-IDF with max_features=15 and unigrams/bigrams. The supplied CSV has 7043 rows and no feedback or support-ticket columns. The app synthesizes those from churn labels, which is target leakage. The notebook uses 500 rows and records 100% accuracy, but this is not valid evidence of generalization. TF-IDF is fitted before the test split in this app, another leakage issue. Describe these as learning projects, not production systems. No live prediction app is hosted here; source ZIP is downloadable.

SMS Spam Detection & NLP Playground is a Streamlit app using NLTK tokenization, punctuation/stopword removal, Porter stemming or WordNet lemmatization, TF-IDF with max_features=2500, and Multinomial Naive Bayes. Features: step-by-step preprocessing, BoW versus TF-IDF, model comparisons, confusion matrices and reports, individual SMS classification, and batch CSV scanning. Dataset has 5572 messages: 4825 ham and 747 spam. Notebook records 97.67% test accuracy for stemming and 97.94% for lemmatization on a stratified 80/20 split with random_state=42. These are saved notebook results, not independently rerun. A ham prediction does not guarantee safety. Source ZIP is downloadable; app is not hosted here.
